subject.title: fix(gateway): support native Windows exec approvals

question: For this remote exec-approval protocol change, should maintainers require current-head Windows companion get/set proof before merge, or accept source-contract and Testbox evidence once the null-metadata blocker is fixed?
rationale: The PR touches a security-sensitive remote exec approval boundary, the author explicitly says no fresh native Windows run is claimed, and automation cannot prove the contributor's native setup for them.

options.title: Require current-head Windows proof
options.body: Hold merge until the nullable metadata fix lands and a redacted native Windows get/set run or logs prove the real companion path.

options.title: Accept source-contract proof after repair
options.body: Maintainers may choose to merge after the null-metadata fix using released-source and Testbox evidence only, while owning the runtime proof gap.

options.title: Fold back into the broader Windows PR
options.body: Pause this focused PR and let the broader Windows approvals and pairing PR carry the remaining proof and integration scope.

recommendation.title: Require current-head Windows proof
recommendation.body: Hold merge until the nullable metadata fix lands and a redacted native Windows get/set run or logs prove the real companion path.

likelyOwner.reason: He has the strongest current-main history on the exec approvals CLI/gateway/protocol path and authored the focused extraction under review.
